data.title: Bucharest’s main North Railway Station looking for artists to restore mural
data.description: CFR, Romania’s state-owned railway company, is looking for artists to restore the mural at platform 14 at Bucharest North Railway Station (Gara de Nord). The project is themed “The History of Romanian Railways at North Railway Station” and aims to reinterpret more than 150 years of railway history through a public artwork, according to Mediafax . Visual artists, graffiti creators, art students, and artistic collectives can propose graffiti, street art, mural painting, or illustration projects, individually or in teams. Selection will take into account the originality of the proposal, the quality of the concept, and respect for historical landmarks. The company specified that no fees, cash prizes, or other financial rewards will be awarded to the winners. The selected artists will contribute voluntarily to the creation of the artwork under a collaboration agreement. CFR will provide the approved surface, facilitate access, and support the promotion of the project, while attracting partners to supply the necessary materials is also being considered. In return, participants will benefit from the exposure of their work at one of Romania’s best-known railway stations, the opportunity to sign it and have their names included on a presentation panel, as well as promotion through the company’s official channels. The deadline for applications is November 13.

data.title: How Often Should You Service Your Car to Keep It Running Smoothly?
data.description: Regular servicing keeps your car safe, efficient and cheaper to run, yet many drivers are unsure when to book one. The short answer: most vehicles need attention every 12 months or 12,000 miles, whichever comes first. Your driving habits, however, can shift that timeline considerably. Here is how to read the intervals, adapt them to your routine, and spot trouble early. The baseline rule: time and mileage intervals For most cars, a full service is due every 12 months or 12,000 miles, whichever arrives first. This full inspection typically covers an oil and filter change, air filter replacement, and a thorough check of the brakes, suspension, steering and safety systems. Drivers who cover high mileage often add an interim service every 6 months or 6,000 miles, a lighter visit focused on oil, fluid levels, tyres and lights. Your owner's manual remains the real authority. Manufacturer schedules vary widely: some modern engines running on synthetic oil can stretch to 18,000 or even 20,000 miles between visits, while others rely on onboard computers that calculate intervals dynamically. Following the manufacturer's schedule also protects your warranty. If your service booklet is missing, digital records can usually be retrieved from the garage or dealership that carried out the work. Treat any interval as a maximum, not a target: servicing slightly early causes no harm, while running late means components operate in conditions they were not designed for. Why low-mileage cars still need annual servicing Time-based intervals exist because fluids degrade chemically, whether or not the car moves. Engine oil oxidises and absorbs moisture, losing its ability to lubricate and protect. Brake fluid is hygroscopic: it steadily absorbs water from the air, which lowers its boiling point and can compromise stopping power. Coolant gradually loses the corrosion inhibitors that protect your radiator and engine internals. Short journeys make things worse. A car driven five miles at a time rarely reaches full operating temperature, so condensation builds up in the oil and exhaust system, the battery never fully recharges, and internal components wear faster than the odometer suggests. Rubber parts, including tyres, belts, hoses and wiper blades, also age with time rather than distance. A car covering only 3,000 miles a year therefore still needs a yearly check. Skipping it because the mileage looks low is one of the most common, and most expensive, mistakes owners make. Driving conditions that shorten your service interval Manufacturers quietly assume "normal" use, but much real-world driving qualifies as severe. Stop-and-go city traffic keeps the engine idling and the brakes working constantly. Frequent trips under five miles, towing a trailer, dusty or unpaved roads, and prolonged heat or freezing cold all accelerate wear on oil, filters, brake pads and the cooling system. If several of these describe your routine, the standard 12-month interval is likely too generous. The practical fix is simple: split the year into two visits. An interim check every 6 months or 6,000 miles catches worn pads, contaminated oil and low fluids before they escalate. Many drivers handle this by booking a service auto package with a professional garage, which keeps inspections consistent and the service history documented. Adjusting frequency to your real driving costs far less than the repairs that follow neglected maintenance. Warning signs your car needs attention sooner Schedules aside, your car communicates directly when something is wrong. Treat any of the following as a prompt to book an inspection, whatever the calendar says: Dashboard warnings, especially the service, oil-pressure or check-engine lights Squealing, grinding or a soft pedal when braking Unusual vibrations, knocking sounds or the car pulling to one side Visible leaks, smoke from the exhaust or a sudden drop in fuel economy Sluggish starting, rough idling or hesitation when accelerating Modern vehicles add another layer: onboard computers monitor oil life and trigger reminders based on actual usage. If a warning appears before the 12-month mark, do not ignore it, because the car is measuring something you cannot see. Between professional visits, basic monthly checks go a long way: oil level, coolant, tyre tread and pressure, lights and wipers. Five minutes in the driveway often prevents the kind of breakdown that ruins a weekend and a budget. Make your next service a habit, not a guess The drivers who spend least on repairs are rarely the luckiest. They are the most consistent. Open your owner's manual today, note the recommended interval, and set a reminder for your next service date. Keep every invoice and stamp in one place: a documented history protects your warranty, strengthens resale value, and turns maintenance from a stressful guess into a routine you never have to think about.

data.title: Romania to get its first Radisson Blu thermal spa resort in Băile Felix
data.description: Winners First, a Romanian hospitality company and operator of Radisson Blu Hotel Cluj, announced the affiliation agreement for the country’s first Radisson thermal resort in Băile Felix. Romania’s only five-star thermal resort, currently operating under the name Lotus Therm Resort & Spa, will undergo a transformation process to align with Radisson Blu’s international standards, with its launch under the new brand scheduled for early in the second quarter of 2027. “Drawing on the experience gained from operating Radisson Blu Hotel Cluj and the synergies between the two properties, we aim to make Radisson Blu Resort & Spa, Felix both a leading destination for premium relaxation, wellness, and longevity stays and a preferred choice for companies looking to organize corporate events and impactful experiences for their teams,” said Nina Moldovan, CEO of Winners First. Radisson Blu Resort & Spa Felix is currently Romania’s only five-star thermal complex. The resort boasts impressive infrastructure, including ten indoor and outdoor swimming pools, the vast majority supplied with natural thermal water, spa and wellness areas, facilities dedicated to families and children, as well as specialized services for recovery and maintaining a healthy lifestyle. The transformation of the complex and its alignment with Radisson Blu’s international standards are already underway and are being carried out in stages through an investment program worth more than EUR 17 million for renovation and modernization. The hotel will remain open throughout the process. The resort’s offering will be complemented by new services and concepts inspired by the Radisson Blu experience. An important stage of the transformation, planned for next year, is the renovation of the Med Spa, in line with the latest international trends in wellness and longevity. The space will feature a contemporary design and an expanded range of treatments and therapies dedicated to relaxation, revitalization, recovery, and well-being. Radisson Blu Resort & Spa Felix has three multifunctional conference rooms, two meeting rooms, and spaces dedicated to corporate events, social events, and private celebrations, offering flexibility for a wide range of formats and experiences. The complex can host conferences, leadership retreats, product launches, and corporate events, combining facilities dedicated to business meetings with personalized services.

Radisson Blu Resort & Spa Felix is currently Romania’s only five-star thermal complex. The resort boasts impressive infrastructure, including ten indoor and outdoor swimming pools, the vast majority supplied with natural thermal water, spa and wellness areas, facilities dedicated to families and children, as well as specialized services for recovery and maintaining a healthy lifestyle. The transformation of the complex and its alignment with Radisson Blu’s international standards are already underway and are being carried out in stages through an investment program worth more than EUR 17 million for renovation and modernization. The hotel will remain open throughout the process. The resort’s offering will be complemented by new services and concepts inspired by the Radisson Blu experience. An important stage of the transformation, planned for next year, is the renovation of the Med Spa, in line with the latest international trends in wellness and longevity. The space will feature a contemporary design and an expanded range of treatments and therapies dedicated to relaxation, revitalization, recovery, and well-being. Radisson Blu Resort & Spa Felix has three multifunctional conference rooms, two meeting rooms, and spaces dedicated to corporate events, social events, and private celebrations, offering flexibility for a wide range of formats and experiences. The complex can host conferences, leadership retreats, product launches, and corporate events, combining facilities dedicated to business meetings with personalized services.

data.title: Bucharest Stock Exchange opens nominations for 2026 edition of flagship program BVB Arena
data.description: The Bucharest Stock Exchange launched the BVB Arena 2026 edition on Wednesday, October 14, targeting Romanian entrepreneurial companies with high growth potential and capital market readiness. Through its redesigned structure, the program aims to identify and select relevant companies while creating a structured framework for direct interaction with capital market professionals. The launch event was officially marked by the traditional bell-ringing ceremony, signaling the start of the nomination phase. Nominations for BVB Arena 2026 can be submitted on the dedicated platform www.bvbarena.ro between October 14 and November 15, 2026. Submissions can be made by members of the Nomination Committee, entrepreneurs (including self-nominations), as well as the public. Eligibility requirements include, among others, a minimum annual turnover threshold of RON 5 million and recorded net profit in each of the last 3 years of operation. Following the nomination stage, the Nomination Committee will vote and select 40 "IPO Candidate" companies to advance to the next phases. These companies will participate in 1-on-1 site visits, facilitating direct dialogue with capital market experts. Based on these visits, individual assessment reports will be drafted. These reports will serve as an analytical tool for the Jury, alongside the other criteria outlined in the methodology, during the final review and voting process. Importantly, the Listing Potential Assessment Sheets do not constitute a listing certification, a due diligence process, or an investment recommendation, and offer no guarantees regarding an eventual listing. Subsequently, a Public Vote will designate 3 "IPO Public Choice" companies, while the Jury will select the 12 "IPO Ready" businesses. The companies selected in these two categories will be announced and awarded at the official BVB Arena Gala. “All the companies that become IPO Candidates in this year's BVB Arena are built, scaled, and led by individuals who made the right calls. They can now engage with BVB Arena's partners— custodians of some of the most valuable economic lessons learned over the last two centuries across every region where market economies took shape and evolved, and key architects of what lies ahead. This interaction will significantly strengthen Romania’s entrepreneurial community,” stated Remus Vulpescu, CEO of the Bucharest Stock Exchange. This year brings several changes to the program. The financial performance of nominated companies will be analyzed within the context of their specific industry, using sector financial benchmarks and a relative performance scoring system.

data.title: Romanian-Turkish Friendship Concert: Violinist Florin Iliescu to perform alongside Istanbul State Symphony Orchestra, Ion Marin conducting
data.description: The Romanian Cultural Institute (ICR) in Istanbul and the Istanbul State Symphony Orchestra will host the Romanian-Turkish Friendship Concert this week, ICR said. The concert, scheduled to take place on October 16 at the Atatürk Cultural Center (AKM), will see Romanian violinist Florin Iliescu performing as guest soloist alongside the Istanbul State Symphony Orchestra under the baton of Romanian conductor Ion Marin. The program will open with Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy’s Violin Concerto in E Minor, Op. 64, and will continue with Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky’s Symphony No. 4 in F Minor, Op. 36. The concert is part of the Turkish orchestra’s official season. Ion Marin's career spans more than four decades on the world’s major stages, from the Berlin Philharmonic, the London Philharmonic Orchestra, and the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra to Teatro alla Scala, the Metropolitan Opera, and Opéra Bastille. Florin Iliescu built an international career both as a soloist and as concertmaster. Since 2018, he has held the position of concertmaster of the Frankfurt Radio Symphony Orchestra. He trained under leading figures in the violin tradition, including Zakhar Bron, Leonidas Kavakos, and Ștefan Gheorghiu. The Istanbul State Symphony Orchestra (IDSO) was founded in 1945 by composer and conductor Cemal Reșit Rey under the name Istanbul City Orchestra. In 1972, it came under the authority of the Ministry of Culture and Tourism and adopted its current name. The orchestra has collaborated over the decades with internationally renowned conductors and soloists, including Aaron Copland, Yehudi Menuhin, Luciano Pavarotti, and Fazıl Say, among many others. It has also given numerous premieres of works by Turkish composers. The orchestra has toured extensively across Europe, the Americas, Asia, and other regions.

data.title: R.Power unveils second utility-scale BESS project in Romania
data.description: European independent power producer R.Power announced on Wednesday, October 14, that it is progressing with its second utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) in Romania and the region. The company’s 100 MW / 200 MWh project, Studina BESS, is located in Olt County, southern Romania. Like the nearby project, Scornicesti (127MW / 254 MWh), which is now nearing completion, Studina is a standalone system that will add significant storage capacity to the Romanian network, supporting grid stability and energy security. The project sits within a wider CEE pipeline that includes 0.9GW / 3GWh of assets in operation and under construction, alongside 0.7 GW / 2.8 GWh of commercialised, ready-to-build projects. R.Power has appointed an experienced contractor to handle Balance of Plant and high-voltage grid connection works for the project, which will connect to the national distribution grid, according to the company press release. Construction is expected to begin in Q4 this year, ahead of an expected connection date in Q3 2027. “Having advanced our flagship Romanian BESS, Scornicesti, through financing, commercialisation and construction, we are now pleased to set the wheels in motion for Studina, which will play an equally important role in supporting the regional energy transition,” said Florin Federenciuc, R.Power Country Head for Romania. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Warsaw, R.Power has evolved from one of the largest renewable energy developers in Central & Eastern Europe into a pan-European IPP, with 1.9GW of projects operational or under construction.

data.title: Central Romania: Făgăraș Fortress attracts three bids for RON 26.3 million restoration project
data.description: Hidro Salt B92 and two consortia, one led by Euras and comprising Dicon Company and Mădbeton, and the other led by Troia Premium Construct and including Proconstruct, have submitted bids for restoration works on several structures at Făgăraș Fortress that were excluded from the previous renovation project. These include the Castle, the North and South Guard Buildings, and the Entrance Gate Tower. The works are financed through European funds and have been estimated at RON 26.3 million, excluding VAT, according to Profit.ro . The list of works includes completing masonry, archaeological excavations, treatments to eliminate moisture, floor restoration, installation of wooden joinery, restoration of stone elements, reinforcement of the roof structure, and roof repairs. Fire safety works, modern installations, and interior finishes adapted to the historical character will also be carried out. In addition, spaces for exhibitions and public interaction will be arranged, along with administrative areas required for the complex’s operation, such as offices, a meeting room, and an archive. The first restoration phase of the Făgăraș Fortress was completed in 2023 following European funding of more than EUR 6.5 million. The project rehabilitated the defensive walls and several bastions, while the wooden bridges were rebuilt in accordance with their 17th-century appearance. Făgăraș Fortress is located in the center of Făgăraș, Brașov County. Construction of the fortress began in 1310 on the site of an older earth-and-wood fortification dating from the 12th century. In 2014, the Fortress was named the second-best castle in the world, according to a list made by Hopper and quoted by Huffington Post .

data.title: Films by four Romanian directors shortlisted for the 39th European Film Awards
data.description: The films of four Romanian directors have been selected for the 39th edition of the European Film Awards, which celebrate “the finest achievements in European cinema.” Cristian Mungiu’s Fjord , also the winner of this year’s Palme d’Or and Romania’s Oscar entry; Alina Şerban’s I Matter , the winner of the Audience Award at this year’s Venice Film Festival; Radu Jude’s The Diary of a Chambermaid , which premiered in this year’s Quinzaine des Cinéastes/Directors’ Fortnight in Cannes; and Florin Şerban’s You Don’t Belong Here , the winner of the Pardo d’Oro at this year’s Locarno Film Festival are on the Fiction Shortlist of the awards. A total of 68 feature films have been shortlisted for a possible nomination for the European Film Awards, with the winners voted for by members of the European Film Academy. Forty-five films are selected for the fiction shortlist, 15 for the documentary shortlist and eight for the animation shortlist. Representing 40 European countries, the films bring together established and emerging filmmakers, including directors working across borders. Twenty-five films are directed or co-directed by women. “Together, they celebrate the excellence, diversity and creativity of European cinema, reflecting its many cultures, languages and perspectives while exploring some of today’s most pressing issues, from migration and cultural clashes to minority communities, gender and political freedom,” the organizers said. The shortlisted fiction and documentary films have been chosen by members of the European Film Academy Board and invited European experts, whereas the shortlisted animated feature films have been chosen by a selection committee composed of members of the Academy Board and invited experts in co-operation with CARTOON, the European Association of Animation Film. The nominations for the categories ‘European Film’, ‘European Discovery - Prix FIPRESCI’, ‘European Documentary’, ‘European Animation Film’, ‘European Director’, ‘European Actress’, ‘European Actor’, ‘European Screenwriter’, ‘European Casting Director’, ‘European Cinematographer’, ‘European Composer (Original Score)’, ‘European Costume Designer’, ‘European Editor’, ‘European Make-Up & Hair Artist’, ‘European Production Designer’ and ‘European Sound’ will be announced on November 14, during the Thessaloniki International Film Festival. The nominations for the ‘European Young Audience Award’ will be announced on November 1, at the International Film Festival Glasgow. On November 13, the nominations for the ‘European Short Film’, selected by the European Film Academy Short Film Network, will be revealed at the Seville European Film Festival. The nominees for the ‘LUX Audience Award’ will be unveiled on November 25.

data.title: Italian-Romanian student wins prize at global essay competition
data.description: Carola Canale, a Year 11 student at the International British School of Bucharest, won third prize at the international competition organized by the John Locke Institute. The awards ceremony took place on October 3 at Grosvenor House in London. The 2026 competition received more than 100,000 essays from 183 countries, according to a press release. Carola Canale’s essay examined the relationship between religiosity and per capita education spending, addressing the question: “Research shows a strong negative correlation between religiosity and per capita spending on education. Is one the cause of the other?” The essay argued that official spending figures do not capture all forms of education, including the role of families, communities, and faith in developing children’s character and values. “The village was never merely a metaphor. It was an alternative theory of education,” the Romanian student wrote, drawing on the proverb “It takes a village to raise a child.” Her analysis considered three possible explanations for the relationship between religion and education spending: economic development, differing views of education and human development, and reverse causality between secular education and declining religious belief. “If education truly means forming wise and fully developed human beings, rather than producing efficient workers, then the most important investments are precisely those that our financial statistics cannot see,” she wrote. Carola Canale said the research process changed her initial view of the topic and ultimately turned the academic argument into a personal conviction. “By the end, I was no longer defending an essay. I was defending what I truly believed,” she concluded.

data.title: Sibiu Gastronomic Week returns in November with 32 restaurants
data.description: The second edition of Sibiu Gastronomic Week will take place from November 2 to 8, bringing together 32 local restaurants. Each venue will offer a special menu featuring two representative dishes for RON 50. The menus will cover traditional Romanian food, international cuisines, and contemporary interpretations, the organizers said. The campaign aims to encourage residents and tourists to try new restaurants and explore Sibiu’s culinary scene. The first edition, held in March 2026, included 26 restaurants and sold more than 6,000 special menus in seven days. “The first edition showed us that Sibiu residents are open to exploring local gastronomy and that restaurants have much to gain when we develop projects together that bring the public closer to them,” said Horațiu Bujac, president of the Sibiu HoReCa Employers’ Organization. “We want Gastronomic Week to become a Sibiu tradition and contribute in the long term to strengthening the city’s culinary identity.” The complete list of participating restaurants is available on the campaign’s website .

data.title: FIDES: Romania needs a national, affordable housing program
data.description: Romania needs a national, affordable housing program, adapted to local needs, and a functional legislative and financial framework, including for public-private partnerships (PPPs) and real estate investment trusts (REITs), participants at the Affordable Housing Summit Romania concluded. “We have one of the highest home-ownership rates in Europe, yet four in ten Romanians live in overcrowded homes. Owning a home is not the same as having the home you need. To move from policies to projects, and from projects to homes people can afford, we need a national program and rules that work, including for public-private partnerships and REITs,” said Constantin Sebeșanu, the president of the Federation of Investors and Developers for a Sustainable Economy (FIDES), an employers’ organization representing real estate developers and related activities. A 55-square-metre flat, bought with a 15% down payment and a 25-year mortgage, would take 56.3% of the average net salary. After the mortgage payment and a minimum cost-of-living basket, an employee on an average income would be left with EUR 47 a month. The analysis, made by the Institute for Visionary Cities (IOV) and presented at the summit, shows the hurdle to home ownership: not at the asking price, but at what is left of a salary once the mortgage is paid. In 2025, 93.2% of Romanians lived in a home owned by their household, the second-highest share in the European Union, and 92% lived in a home of their own with no loan on it, according to data presented at the summit. At the same time, 40.4% lived in overcrowded homes, against an EU average of 16.8%, the highest rate in the Union. Arrears on rent, mortgage, utility bills or hire purchase doubled in four years, from 9.4% in 2021 to 18.5% in 2025, the steepest increase in the EU. “Housing is relatively affordable. Financing it is not,” was the conclusion of the presentation by Florian Filat, Executive Director of IOV. The 56.3% payment in the model exceeds the 45% ceiling that the National Bank of Romania allows for a first home. The Colliers presentation by Gabriel Blăniță, Director, Valuation & Advisory Services, Colliers Romania, added to the picture: only 1% of Romanians live in a home with an outstanding mortgage and 7% rent, compared with 27% and 35% respectively in the euro area. Matthew Baldwin, Head of the European Commission’s Task Force on Housing, said that housing is a fundamental right, not a privilege. It is also an issue for the economy and for jobs, including labor mobility, the European official added. Baldwin encouraged Romania to be the first country in the region to launch such a program. The summit’s conclusions recommend that large employers and employers’ confederations bring hard labor-market data on where housing costs are holding back recruitment and retention, including for teachers, doctors, police officers and other essential workers. In Romania, public-private partnerships were designed for large infrastructure. FIDES said it supports a public-private partnership framework adapted to housing projects, “with risks and benefits clearly allocated and with the impact on the public budget assessed transparently for each model, as well as the adoption, promulgation and implementation of the law on real estate investment companies, currently going through the legislative process in the Chamber of Deputies.” REITs could bring long-term capital into rental housing, in a country where renting is still the exception, the organization said. Cohesion Policy 2021–2027 supports investment in social and affordable housing worth EUR 500.5 million in EU funds, of which EUR 206.5 million was redirected to the sector through the mid-term review, according to the Ministry of Investments and European Projects. Access to these funds is not automatic: it depends on the rules of each program, on the eligibility of investments and on well-prepared projects. Dragoș Pîslaru, the interim Minister of Investments and European Projects, said that what is really missing in Romania right now is a coordinated vision for the housing sector. The next step, in the minister’s view, is a shift from direct public funding to mechanisms that attract private capital.

The summit’s conclusions recommend that large employers and employers’ confederations bring hard labor-market data on where housing costs are holding back recruitment and retention, including for teachers, doctors, police officers and other essential workers. In Romania, public-private partnerships were designed for large infrastructure. FIDES said it supports a public-private partnership framework adapted to housing projects, “with risks and benefits clearly allocated and with the impact on the public budget assessed transparently for each model, as well as the adoption, promulgation and implementation of the law on real estate investment companies, currently going through the legislative process in the Chamber of Deputies.” REITs could bring long-term capital into rental housing, in a country where renting is still the exception, the organization said. Cohesion Policy 2021–2027 supports investment in social and affordable housing worth EUR 500.5 million in EU funds, of which EUR 206.5 million was redirected to the sector through the mid-term review, according to the Ministry of Investments and European Projects. Access to these funds is not automatic: it depends on the rules of each program, on the eligibility of investments and on well-prepared projects. Dragoș Pîslaru, the interim Minister of Investments and European Projects, said that what is really missing in Romania right now is a coordinated vision for the housing sector. The next step, in the minister’s view, is a shift from direct public funding to mechanisms that attract private capital.

data.title: AccessABILITY Expo returns to Bucharest with focus on AI and workplace inclusion
data.description: The Romanian Diversity Chamber of Commerce (RDCC) is set to hold the third edition of AccessABILITY between October 22 and 23 at the National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest, AN building. Over the course of two days, the event will bring together people with disabilities and their families, public authorities, non-governmental organizations, and specialists in technology, education, and healthcare.  Attendance is free upon registration. According to the organizers, AccessABILITY Expo 2026 aims to create a space where solutions can be discovered and tested: the firsthand experiences of people with disabilities are part of the innovation process, while companies, institutions, and the wider community can build partnerships and remove barriers. “This year, we are taking another step forward: bringing together the community, the business sector, institutions, technology, and a new generation of innovators to address real-world challenges. Accessibility should not be viewed as an exception or as a separate project, but as an integral part of the way we build products, services, workplaces, and communities,” said Lestat Monroe, founder of the Romanian Diversity Chamber of Commerce (RDCC). More than a quarter of the people with disabilities experience severe material and social deprivation in Romania. According to the latest Eurostat data, the percentage reached 26.7% in 2024, the second-highest rate in the European Union. The AccessABILITY Expo exhibition area will bring together solutions across fields such as assistive technology, accessible mobility and transportation, inclusive recruitment, smart living, digital accessibility and AI, healthcare and rehabilitation, education, sports, culture and tourism. Visitors will be able to interact directly with providers and test products and technologies that can contribute to greater independence and participation in everyday life. One of the highlights of the 2026 edition is the AI Accessibility Hackathon, a 24-hour competition in which student teams will develop AI-powered applications and solutions to address real-world challenges faced by people with disabilities. The organizers encourage the formation of diverse teams that include people with disabilities, ensuring the lived experience of those who will use these solutions is integrated from the very beginning of the development process. On October 22, AccessABILITY Expo will also host a new edition of Romanian Accessibility Awareness Day – RAAD, the conference dedicated to accessibility and inclusion at the workplace. Under the theme “From access to belonging”, business leaders, HR professionals, accessibility specialists, and people with lived experience will explore three essential dimensions of inclusive organizations: accessible systems, psychological safety, and wellbeing. The professional program is complemented by the workshop “Disability inclusion in the workplace: from barriers to action,” a practical session for HR professionals, managers, and business leaders.

data.title: Romanian co-founded tech company Opaque acquired by Anthropic
data.description: Opaque, a company co-founded by Romanian Raluca Ada Popa, announced that it had been acquired by Anthropic, the developer of Claude, after the two companies reached an agreement. Opaque essentially helps organizations to run AI workloads on sensitive data with hardware-enforced protections. “As AI evolved, so did the problem we set out to solve. Protecting data and models was no longer enough. Organizations also needed a way to independently verify how AI systems and agents behaved. This led us to expand our work from confidential AI to verifiable AI: replacing assumptions of trust with cryptographic evidence of what ran, where it ran, and under which policies,” the company explained in a press release. The team at Opaque developed technology and contributed to open-source projects aimed at security, governance, and verifiability in the AI sector. “We also saw this work expanding beyond OPAQUE. Through AgenTrust and projects such as Agent Governance Toolkit, TRACE, Confidential MCP, and Weight Custody Manifest, we have collaborated with a broader community to develop open approaches to some of the most difficult trust and security challenges arising around AI agents and models,” the company further explained. Popa is the co-founder and president of Opaque Systems, and she is also an associate professor at the University of California, Berkeley. “Anthropic is acquiring Opaque, the company I co-founded with my students at Berkeley and a colleague,” Raluca Ada Popa announced on her Facebook page. https://www.facebook.com/raluca.ada/posts/pfbid0GexCUguHuoUfEX15DvpkyVECV5zgoSNH5iy8ejTLy3wLEfVpchtPZMmQR84DEoF2l

data.title: Bucharest airports automate free parking access for people with reduced mobility
data.description: Bucharest Airports National Company (CNAB) announced on Wednesday, October 14, that it introduced automated parking access for vehicles transporting people with reduced mobility who hold valid permits. The system is available in the public parking lots at both airports serving the Romanian capital. License plate recognition technology checks each arriving vehicle against a dedicated database. If the registration is valid, the barrier opens automatically without requiring a parking ticket or staff assistance, according to CNAB. The company said the system is intended to “reduce formalities and provide people with reduced mobility with predictable, simple, and fast access to airport infrastructure.” “To obtain automated access, eligible individuals or their representatives must send the required registration information to parcare.pmr@cnab.ro: the full name of the beneficiary or legal representative, details of the reduced-mobility permit, the vehicle’s license plate number, and contact information,” reads the official announcement. The original reduced-mobility permit must remain clearly displayed at the front of the vehicle while it is parked. Changes to the registered license plate or extensions to the permit’s validity must be reported at least 48 hours in advance. If the system does not recognize a registered vehicle, drivers can use the intercom at the barrier. Airport staff will then verify the information and authorize access, the company said.

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: APANHA-SE MAIS DEPRESSA UM MENTIROSO QUE UM COXO!
data.description:
DSP através da sua equipa de "Lambe-Botas" está cavando cada vez mais a sua própria cova, adiantando cada vez mais o seu fim. Somente alguns acreditavam que foi ele quem estava por trás do "Progresso Nacional" o blog onde começou toda essa história de Mentiras, Calunias, Difamações, Ameaças e tantos outros agressões tóxicas ao espírito humano, a todos os que não estão do seu lado e cujo o único objectivo, era ser chamado de rei dos réis da Guiné. Comandou o Progresso Nacional assim como Bin Laden comandou a Al-Qaeda e acabou por fracassar. Pensou, repensou e resolveu voltar novamente ainda com mais TERROR e está a comandar o Guiné Puro tentando levar toda a nação ao abismo assim como o ISIS quer levar a humanidade. Camaradas, Guiné Puro assim como o falecido Progresso Nacional é o reflexo do espirito de DSP, alí é possivel ver tudo e quanto o sujeito é baixo. DSP é um hipócrita e um anarquista moderno. "ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E COMPRAS?!" essa foi uma das frases da recente publicação que mostram por quem e para que fim, é dirigido o Guiné Puro ou melhor o blog do terror como podem ver já a seguir. Demonstraram mais uma vez claramente que o "MCCI" pertence a DPS, pois uma publicação dessa no próprio blog do ganancioso só pode ser das duas uma: "Boca capli elis ou Foronta passanta e dicidi ca sucundi rostu". Camaradas, Domingos Simões Pereira afundou seu próprio barco devido a sua ganância e complexo de superioridade. "I pirigu pa i faladu ba cuma, el i unicu alguim cu bai escola na Guiné" seu ultimo desejo é "afundar com todos, inclusive o PAIGC". __________PARA A VOSSA CONFIRMAÇÃO, AQUI ESTÁ A PUBLICAÇÃO_________ MARCOS GALINA BARBOSA VAI PERCEBER QUE METEU COM GENTE
PERSISTENTE. BÔ DISSAL I NA BIN FASSI PASSSAÇÃO LI. tUDO PUBLICAÇÕES KU I FASSI
I NA RESP+UNDI PAREL. NIN IKANA SEDU DIDIA. NONA VINGAL MANERA KU NÓ PUDI. JÁ
TEMOS ALGUÉM NO AEROPORTO PARA NOS INFOMAR O DIA EM QUE EL CHEGAR. INVENTOU
AGRESSÃO E NESTE MOMENTO ESTÁ EM QUELUZ EM PORTUGAL. FILHO DA PUTA. MENTIROSO
COMO OS TEUS PATRÕES OS SUJOS JOMAV E BRAIMA CAMARÁ. MARCOS GALINA, BU NA
ARREPENDI. PERA BU DJUBI. ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E
COMPRAS?! VAMOS PROVAR DEPOIS. FIDJU DI BALETA Olá a todos, ainda bem que descobriram
que o Pirata informático- hackec é o Marcos Galina Barbosa, Eng. Informático.
Tentei várias vezes avisar o Ticha Aly Silva mas ele não respondeu e nem deu
importância julgo eu. No tempo da campanha para a liderança do Paigc, este
indivíduo era um fervoroso apoiante do Bá Quecuto no Facebook e a técnica que
usava era o envio de Phishing aos apoiantes do Dsp, recolhia informações
pessoais das pessoas que posteriormente eram expostas no Blog do Doka. Tentou
comigo mas não resultou. Tenham cuidado com este sujeito que está nas mãos de
B. Camara. Outra coisa, gostaria de conhecer a vossa página no Fecebook. Estamos Juntos. AC Nota GP: Até jovens inocentes,
Lesmes, Masta Tito e demais outros, os tais vendidos e comprados foram as tuas
vítimas. teu filho da puta que o bandido de Baciro Djá trouxe para Bissau para funções no aparelho de Estado e dizes que outros recebem favores.
Desde quando é que és mais honesto ou
mais competentes que os outros? Pagas e até pode ser com a tua vida para
perceberes as irresponsabilidades
dos teus actos. Publicada por O

data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13
